config.title: useToggle

intro.title: useToggle
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useToggle` that manages a boolean state. You will learn how to encapsulate stateful logic into a reusable function, a core concept in React for writing clean and maintainable code. The main technologies involved are React's `useState` hook and TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll have a handy hook you can use in any component to easily toggle between true and false values.
intro.usecase: The `useToggle` custom hook is a fundamental pattern for managing binary UI states across countless real-world applications. Developers use it to control the visibility of modals, sidebars, and dropdown menus in dashboards and admin panels. It's essential for handling on/off states in interactive features like dark mode switches, expandable filters, and accordion panels within forms. This hook encapsulates the repetitive logic of toggling a boolean, making code cleaner and more maintainable in any component that needs a simple switch.

objectives: Implement a custom useToggle hook that manages boolean state
Initialize the useToggle hook with a default boolean value
Configure the hook to return both the current state and toggle functions
Bind the toggle function to UI event handlers
Update component state using the toggle functionality
Integrate the useToggle hook into a functional component
Render dynamic UI elements based on the toggle state

successCriteria: useState is called with false, and the result is destructured into a state variable and setter function inside useToggle.

steps.instruction: Inside the useToggle function, define a function named toggle that calls setState with the opposite of the current state value.
